Keysight Technologies Inc serves technology innovators as a mission-critical design enablement partner for complex engineering challenges across AI infrastructure, communications, industrial automation, aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductor, and general electronics [D1]. The company reported record third quarter fiscal 2026 results for the period ended July 31, 2026, with revenue of $1.85 billion against $1.35 billion a year earlier [D1]. GAAP net income was $397 million, or $2.30 per diluted share, compared with $191 million, or $1.10 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2025 [D1]. Non-GAAP net income was $531 million, or $3.07 per diluted share, against $297 million, or $1.72, a year earlier [D1]. Orders rose 56% to $2.09 billion, the second consecutive record quarter with orders over $2 billion [D1]. Cash flow from operations was $437 million and free cash flow was $403 million, compared with $322 million and $291 million a year earlier [D1]. Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $2.62 billion as of July 31, 2026 [D1].

The Communications Solutions Group reported revenue of $1.35 billion, up 43%, reflecting 56% growth in commercial communications and 14% growth in aerospace, defense, and government [D1]. Its income from operations was $458 million against $246 million a year earlier [D1]. The Electronic Industrial Solutions Group reported revenue of $501 million, up 21%, with income from operations of $155 million against $92 million [D1]. Management attributed the growth to the rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem, with wireline orders more than doubling year over year and wireline revenue exceeding wireless for the first time [D3]. Management guided the fourth fiscal quarter to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on a weighted diluted share count of approximately 172 million shares, a revenue mid-point representing year-over-year growth of approximately 37% [D1].

Analysts on the call pressed on whether demand is sustainable and whether supply constraints are limiting guidance, a tone the summary described as slightly negative to pressing [D3]. Management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply and called the supply chain the governor of near-term revenue, with conversion of that demand into revenue likely to be nonlinear for several quarters [D3]. Management also said the one-time tariff impacts this year artificially pulled up fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat [D3]. Management said the supply environment is less flexible than a year earlier and that it is taking an 18-month-plus view of supply chain planning, including product redesigns to accommodate second-source components [D3]. The wireline mix shifted from about 80/20 toward more like 70/30 and recently to probably more like 2/3 and 1/3 as AI data centre build-outs scale [D3]. Hyperscalers are roughly 10% of the business directly [D3].

The mean of 12 short-term price targets is $418.42, indicating a potential upside of 30% from a close of $321.87, with a standard deviation of $19.48 [D5]. The lowest target of $390.00 indicates a 21.2% increase and the most optimistic target of $452.00 indicates a 40.4% increase [D5]. The same write-up notes that price targets mislead investors far more often than they guide and are often set to drum up interest in shares of companies whose firms have existing business relationships or are looking to be associated with them [D5]. Management expects fiscal 2026 revenue growth of 32% and earnings per share growth of approximately 60% at the mid-point [D3]. Integration of the acquired businesses, including Spirent, is largely complete and finished one quarter ahead of schedule, with 80% to 90% of the $100 million cost synergy target expected on a run-rate basis exiting the fiscal year [D3]. Management said the 6G opportunity is greater than the 5G opportunity, with customers moving into funded development programs and a 2029 standard timeline [D3]. Keysight announced a research collaboration with the Centre for Assuring Autonomy at the University of York on AI safety assurance for software-defined vehicles [D7].
